about: A maiden, Xquic, the daughter of Cuchumaquic, one of the lords of Xibalba, hears her father tell of the tree whose fruit appeared when Hunhunahpu's head was set in it, and she goes alone to see it. The skull in the branches speaks: the round fruits are only skulls. She asks for one anyway, and the skull spits into her right hand; the spittle vanishes, and the head explains that a man's sons are his spittle and slaver, so that the face of a lord or a wise man is never lost. Back at home she conceives the twins Hunahpu and Xbalanque. After six months her father sees that she is with child; the lords order her questioned and, when she denies it, sacrificed, and the four owl messengers are sent to bring back her heart in a bowl. On the way she persuades them to spare her, and the red sap of a tree, called the Chuh Q'aq' Che, is put in the bowl in place of her heart. In return she promises the owls a place on the face of the earth. The lords burn the false heart and stand entranced by the sweet smell of its smoke, while the owls lead the maiden up out of Xibalba. So the lords of Xibalba were brought low by a maiden, and all of them blinded.

sentences.t: Va chi cute vꜩihoxic hun capoh, vmeal hun ahau, Cuchumaquic vbi.
sentences.l: This (chi) then its-telling a maiden, his-daughter a lord, Cuchumaquic his-name.
sentences.i: Here, then, is the story of a maiden, the daughter of a lord named Cuchumaquic.
sentences.n: Ximénez's own indented heading, the one the last part announced (Va cute xchi ca biyh roponic 'now we shall tell of her coming'). The manuscript reads Va chi cute (MS vachicute, checked at 2.5×, as Brasseur has it). Va 'this' points forward; chi is not clear here and is left unrendered (perhaps chic 'now, again', its c shared with cute 'then'). vꜩihoxic 'its being told': v- 'its' + ꜩihoh 'tell' + passive -x + -ic. hun capoh 'a maiden' (toggle q'apoj, as in the last part). vmeal 'his daughter': v- 'his' + meal, a man's daughter (the modern word is mi'al; the toggle keeps Ximénez's vowels, umeal). Cuchumaquic is one of the lords of Xibalba named in an earlier part; Brasseur reads cuchuma + quic 'gathered blood' (kept as a name).

sentences.t: Arecut ta xuta hun capoh, vmeal hun ahau, Cuchumaquic vbi vcahau, Xquic cut vbi ri capoh,
sentences.l: This-then when she-heard-it a maiden, his-daughter a lord, Cuchumaquic his-name her-father, Xquic then her-name the maiden,
sentences.i: Now a maiden heard it, the daughter of a lord: Cuchumaquic was her father's name, and Xquic was the maiden's name;
sentences.n: Arecut 'this then' is are 'this is' + cut 'then' written as one word (toggle Arek'ut, as Catecut is K'atek'ut); the paragraph is indented in the manuscript. xuta 'she heard it': x- (completed action) + v- 'she' + ta 'hear', as the last part's xuta. vcahau 'her father': cahau is 'father' (with the possessive), ahau 'lord' on its own. Xquic is the maiden's name; Brasseur's note takes it as the prefix x (or ix), which makes a woman's name, + quic 'blood' or 'rubber' ('sang ou gomme élastique'), and his introduction renders the name 'la Femme-Sang ou la Gomme-Noire' (inferred; the toggle gives Xkik', with the ejective of the known word kik'). The name stays K'iche' in the English.

sentences.t: ta xuta cut vꜩihoxic ri vvach che, ta chi ꜩihox chic rumal vcahau;
sentences.l: when she-heard-it then its-telling the its-fruit tree, when it-is-told again by her-father;
sentences.i: she heard the story of the fruit of the tree when it was told again by her father,
sentences.n: ri vvach che 'the fruit of the tree': vvach is 'its face' and also 'its fruit', the face a tree shows. The tree is the calabash in which Hunhunahpu's head was set at the end of the last part. ta chi ꜩihox chic 'when it was told again': chi + ꜩihox (the passive of ꜩihoh 'tell', without -ic), chic 'again'. rumal 'by' names the teller.

sentences.t: chumaihah cut ta chi ꜩihoxic.
sentences.l: she-marvels-at-it then when it-is-told.
sentences.i: and she marvelled at it as it was told.
sentences.n: chumaihah 'she marvels at it': ch- + v- 'she' + maihah 'marvel at' (inferred, as in the last part's xumaihah, after Brasseur). ta chi ꜩihoxic 'as it is told' repeats the verb of the line before, now with -ic.

sentences.t: “Ma quinaoh vila ri che ca bixic? Quiꜩih quz vvach, ca cha ca nu tao,” xꜭha cut.
sentences.l: “Not I-go(?) I-see-it the tree it-is-said? Truly sweet(?) its-fruit, they-say, I-hear-it,” she-said then.
sentences.i: “Shall I not go (?) and see this tree they speak of? Truly its fruit is sweet, they say, so I hear,” she said.
sentences.n: The maiden speaks to herself. Ma opens a question. quinaoh is a doubtful division (MS ma | quinaoh vila; Brasseur Maquina oh v'ila): quin- is c- + in 'I', and the rest is not clear; 'go' is a guess after Brasseur ('Pourquoi n'irais-je pas voir cet arbre'), and the toggle respells the letters. vila 'I see it': v- 'I' + il 'see' + -a (earlier vila was 'look, you (pl.)'; here the person is 'I'). ca bixic 'it is said, they talk of it' (bih 'say' + passive). In bixic the x is written over another letter, with a second mark above the line; it is read with Brasseur (doubtful). quz is written with plain qu where Brasseur has guz (his g is ꜫ); 'sweet' is inferred from Brasseur ('savoureux') and from the smell in ¶19, and the toggle respells the letters (kus). ca cha ca nu tao 'they say, I hear it' (MS cacha canu tao, divided by us): cha, the quotative 'say'; ca nu tao 'I hear it', ca- ongoing + nu- 'I' + ta 'hear' + -o.

sentences.t: Cate xbec xa vtuquel, xapon cut chuxe che, tiquil chi Pucbal Chah, tiquil vi.
sentences.l: Then she-went only alone, she-arrived-there then at-its-foot tree, planted at Pucbal Chah, planted there.
sentences.i: So she went all alone, and she came to the foot of the tree that stood at Pucbal Chah, stood there.
sentences.n: Cate 'then'. xbec 'she went' (MS b, where Brasseur reads x-pec). xa vtuquel 'only alone, all by herself'. xapon 'she arrived there': x- + apon 'arrive (away from the speaker)'. chuxe che 'at the foot of the tree' (chi + v- 'its' + xe 'root, foot'). tiquil 'planted, standing' (tic 'plant' + -il), as in the last part; it is written with a t–i ligature that can look like ꜩh, as vtihobal was in an earlier part. Pucbal Chah is the place where the brothers were buried (Brasseur 'le Cendrier'). tiquil vi 'planted there' repeats the word, with vi pointing back to the place. After vi the manuscript has a small cross, apparently a reference mark to a later marginal note at the left of the column a few lines below (a cross and a few words); neither is printed.

sentences.t: “Hiiaa! Naquipe vvach vae che?
sentences.l: “Hiiaa! What-is its-fruit this tree?
sentences.i: “Ah! What kind of fruit does this tree bear?
sentences.n: Hiiaa is a cry of wonder, printed as written (Brasseur Hiyaa). Naquipe 'what is', the naquipa of earlier parts with e (toggle Naqipe). vvach vae che 'the fruit of this tree' (vae 'this').

sentences.t: Ma qui pa quz chi vachin va che?
sentences.l: Not how (pa) sweet(?) that it-bears-fruit this tree?
sentences.i: Is it not sweet, the fruit this tree bears?
sentences.n: MS maquipa | quz, divided by us. Ma … pa makes a question, 'is it not …?'. qui is taken as the word of degree 'how, so' of earlier parts (inferred). quz 'sweet' as in ¶3 (Brasseur guz; inferred, toggle kus). vachin 'bear fruit': vach 'fruit' made a verb with -in, the xvachin 'it bore fruit' of the last part (toggle wachin). va che 'this tree'.

sentences.t: Ma qui cam tah, ma qui zach tah laquita xchin chup hunoc,” xꜭha cu ri capoh.
sentences.l: Not I(?)-die may-it, not I(?)-am-lost may-it, laquita(?) I-shall pick(?) one?” she-said then the maiden.
sentences.i: Surely I shall not die, surely I shall not be lost, if I pick just one?” said the maiden.
sentences.n: A couplet: ma qui cam tah, ma qui zach tah 'may I not die, may I not be lost' (MS maqui cam | tah, maqui zachtah). tah, the particle of wish after ma, as in earlier parts; cam 'die' (toggle kam, not k'am 'take'); zach 'be lost, undone'. qui is taken as c- + i(n) 'I', with Brasseur, who reads ma-qu'i and renders 'Mourrai-je donc et sera-ce ma ruine si j'en cueille un?' (inferred). laquita is not otherwise known; 'if' is inferred from Brasseur. xchin 'I shall' (xchi- + in). chup 'pick' is a guess after Brasseur ('cueille'); the same letters give chupel 'put out, extinguished' in ¶7. hunoc 'one' (hun + -oc).

sentences.t: Ta xꜭhau cut ri bac ꜭo vla xol che:
sentences.l: Then it-spoke then the bone there-is hither among tree:
sentences.i: Then the skull that was there among the branches spoke:
sentences.n: xꜭhau 'it spoke' (ꜭhau 'speak'). ri bac 'the bone': here the skull, Hunhunahpu's head set in the tree in the last part (Brasseur 'la tête de mort'). ꜭo vla 'which is there' (ꜭo 'there is', vla 'hither'; MS g-shaped, read ꜭ, as Brasseur's qo ula). xol che 'among the tree, in its branches'.

sentences.t: “Naquipa ca raih chire?
sentences.l: “What you-want to-it?
sentences.i: “What is it you want?
sentences.n: Naquipa 'what'. ca raih 'you want': c- (ongoing) + a- 'you' + raih 'want', the verb of que rah 'they want' in an earlier part (inferred; Brasseur 'Est-ce donc que tu en désires?'). In ca nu raih 'I want it' below, raih takes nu- 'I', so the r belongs to the stem here. chire 'of it, to it'.

sentences.t: Ri xa bac ri colocoxinac chu cabtac che,” xꜭha ri vholom Hunahpu, ta xꜭhauic chire ri capoh.
sentences.l: The only bone the made-round on its-arms tree,” he-said the his-head Hunahpu, when he-spoke to-her the maiden.
sentences.i: Those round things in the branches of the tree are nothing but skulls,” said the head of Hunahpu, speaking to the maiden.
sentences.n: Ri xa bac 'the (things are) only bones'. colocoxinac 'made round' is built on coloc 'round' (the colocac of the last part) with -inac, the ending of a completed state (inferred; Brasseur 'ces boules rondes'; toggle kolokoxinaq). chu cabtac che 'on the arms of the tree', its branches: cab 'arm, hand' + tac, the plural (Brasseur gab-tak). Ximénez writes plain c; the toggle gives q'ab'taq because q'ab' 'hand' is certain. The manuscript has Hunahpu here (ri vholom hunahpu), although the head is Hunhunahpu's: the text itself calls it the head of Hunhunahpu in ¶7 and ¶13, and Brasseur prints Hunhun-Ahpu here too. The name is printed as written, as the fifth part printed Hunhunahpu where the actor was Hunahpu, and the English follows the manuscript. xꜭhauic 'he spoke' (ꜭhau + -ic).

sentences.t: “Ma ca raih?” xuꜭhaxic.
sentences.l: “Not you-want?” she-was-told.
sentences.i: “Do you not want it?” she was asked.
sentences.n: Ma ca raih 'do you not want it?', the question of the line before turned round (Brasseur 'En veux-tu toujours?'). xuꜭhaxic 'she was spoken to': x- + v- + ꜭha 'say' + passive -x + -ic.

sentences.t: “Ca nu raih,” xꜭha cut ri capoh.
sentences.l: “I-want-it,” she-said then the maiden.
sentences.i: “I want it,” said the maiden.
sentences.n: ca nu raih 'I want it': ca- (ongoing) + nu- 'I' + raih 'want'.

sentences.t: “Vꜩ bala; chaliquiba vloc ri a vi qui cab vila na,” xꜭha ri bac.
sentences.l: “Good bala; stretch-it-out hither the your right hand, I-see-it first,” it-said the bone.
sentences.i: “Very well; stretch out your right hand to me, so I may see it,” said the skull.
sentences.n: Vꜩ bala 'very well', as in the house table. chaliquiba 'stretch it out': ch- (command) + a- 'you' + liquiba, liq 'stretch, spread' + -iba (inferred, after Brasseur 'étends'; toggle chalikib'a). ri a vi qui cab 'your right hand' (MS ri avi quicab): vi qui cab is the word for the right hand, as in an earlier part's hun cha vi qui cab 'one on your right'; cab 'hand' is written with plain c, Brasseur gab (toggle q'ab', the certain word). Brasseur reads vi here as 'tip' ('étends seulement le bout de ta main'); the 'right hand' of the earlier part (inferred there) is kept. vila na 'that I may see it first' (v- 'I' + il 'see'; na 'first').

sentences.t: “Ve,” xꜭha cu capoh;
sentences.l: “Yes,” she-said then maiden;
sentences.i: “Yes,” said the maiden,
sentences.n: Ve 'yes', as in an earlier part (Brasseur 'Oui').

sentences.t: xuliquiba acan oc vvi qui cab chuvach bac.
sentences.l: she-stretched-it-out up (oc) her-right hand before-its-face bone.
sentences.i: and she stretched her right hand up before the skull.
sentences.n: xuliquiba 'she stretched it out': x- + v- 'she' + liquiba (MS xuliqui|ba). acan oc 'upward': acan 'climb, go up' with oc, the ending of direction (toggle aq'an oq, as in earlier parts). vvi qui cab 'her right hand', v- 'her' + vi qui cab (toggle uwi ki q'ab'). chuvach bac 'before the skull'.

sentences.t: Catecut chi piꜩ ca ban vchub bac, ta xpetic tacal cut pa cab capoh;
sentences.l: Then with squirt(?) it-is-done its-spittle bone, when it-came landing then in hand maiden;
sentences.i: Then the skull spat out its spittle with force (?), and it came and landed right in the maiden's hand;
sentences.n: chi piꜩ ca ban 'it is done with a squirt (?)': piꜩ is not otherwise known; 'spat with force' follows Brasseur ('lança avec effort un crachat'), a guess, toggle by the letters. vchub bac 'the spittle of the bone': chub 'spittle', the vchub of an earlier part. xpetic 'it came' (pet 'come'). tacal 'landing, coming to rest', as in earlier parts (inferred). pa cab capoh 'in the maiden's hand' (cab with plain c; toggle q'ab').

sentences.t: ta xril cut vpa cab huzuc xunicoh; ma cu habi vchub bac pu cab.
sentences.l: when she-saw-it then its-inside hand at-once she-examined-it(?); not then there-was its-spittle bone in-her hand.
sentences.i: she looked at once into the palm of her hand and searched it, but the skull's spittle was not in her hand.
sentences.n: xril 'she saw it': x- + r- 'she' (the form before a vowel) + il 'see'. vpa cab 'the inside of her hand', her palm: pa 'belly, inside' (the a of pa is written over another letter; Brasseur u pa gab). huzuc 'at once'. xunicoh 'she looked closely at it' is inferred from Brasseur ('jetant un coup d'œil curieux'); nicoh is not otherwise known (toggle xunikoj). ma cu habi 'but there was not' (MS macuhabi, the cu written over another letter). pu cab 'in her hand', pu for pa v- 'in its' (Brasseur's note in an earlier part). The spittle has gone into her: it is the seed of the boys.

sentences.t: “Xa retal mi xnu ya chave ri nu chub, nu caxah.
sentences.l: “Only its-sign just I-gave to-you the my-spittle, my-slaver.
sentences.i: “It is only a sign I have given you, my spittle, my slaver.
sentences.n: The head explains what it has done; the speech runs to the end of the paragraph. Xa retal 'only its sign': r- 'its' + etal 'sign', the vetal of an earlier part (MS xare,tal with a stray comma-like mark). mi xnu ya 'I have just given' (mi 'just now' + x- + nu- 'I' + ya 'give'). chave 'to you': chi + a- 'you' + -ve. nu chub, nu caxah 'my spittle, my slaver' is a couplet, as vchub, vcaxah in an earlier part (toggle chub', kaxaj).

sentences.t: Are ri nu holom mahabi ca chocon chi vi; xa bac, mahabi chi vchac.
sentences.l: This the my-head not-there-is it-serves any-more there; only bone, not-there-is any-more its-flesh(?).
sentences.i: This head of mine is of no more use: it is only bone, it has no flesh any more (?).
sentences.n: mahabi ca chocon chi vi 'it is of no more use': chocon 'serve, be of use' (the choconic of an earlier part), chi for chic 'any more', here and in mahabi chi vchac (Brasseur ma-habi ca chokon chivi; toggle chik). xa bac 'only bone'. vchac is read 'its flesh' with Brasseur ('qui n'a déjà plus de chair'), a guess: the same letters are vchac 'its work' in the sixth part and vchac 'his younger brother' in the last, and 'it has no work any more' would also fit the line before. The toggle respells the letters (uchak).

sentences.t: Xavi quehe vholom ve qui nim ahau; xa vtiohil vꜩ vi vvach.
sentences.l: Also thus his-head if they great lord; only its-flesh good there its-face.
sentences.i: So too is the head of great lords: it is only the flesh that makes the face fair.
sentences.n: Xavi quehe 'just so, so too'. ve qui nim ahau 'if (they are) great lords' (MS vequinimaha with a blot over the last letters; read with Brasseur, ve qui nim ahau): even the heads of great lords. vtiohil 'its flesh' (tiohil 'flesh', as in earlier parts) is a doubtful reading: the t–i ligature looks like vhohil, and it is read with Brasseur (u tiohil). vꜩ vi vvach 'good there its face', what makes the face good to look at.

sentences.t: Arecut ta chi camic chuxibih chi rih vinac rumal vbaquil.
sentences.l: This-then when that he-dies it-frightens behind people because-of its-boniness.
sentences.i: And so, when a man dies, people take fright at him because of his bones.
sentences.n: ta chi camic 'when (one) dies'. chuxibih 'it frightens': ch- + v- + xibih 'frighten', the verb of an earlier part (toggle chuxib'ij). chi rih vinac 'behind people', taken as 'upon people' (inferred; Brasseur 'la terreur qui assiège les hommes au moment de la mort'). vbaquil 'its boniness, its bones': bac 'bone' + -il, the abstract ending (toggle ub'aqil).

sentences.t: Quehe cut xa vꜭahol, queheri vchub vcaxah vꜭoheic, ve vꜭahol ahau, ve puch vꜭahol naol, ahuchan;
sentences.l: Thus then only his-son, like his-spittle his-slaver its-being, if his-son lord, if also his-son wise-one, speaker;
sentences.i: So it is with a son: he is like spittle and slaver, whether he is the son of a lord or the son of a wise man, of an orator;
sentences.n: Quehe cut 'so then'. xa vꜭahol 'only his son' (ꜭahol 'a man's son'; MS g-shaped, read ꜭ). queheri vchub vcaxah vꜭoheic 'like spittle and slaver is his being': the couplet of the first line comes back. ve … ve puch 'whether … or'. naol 'one who knows, a wise man': na 'know, feel' + agent -ol (Brasseur 'artiste'; inferred). ahuchan 'speaker, orator': ah- 'one who' + uchan, taken as a word for speech (Brasseur 'orateur'; inferred, toggle by the letters).

sentences.t: xma chi zach vi chi bec, chi ꜩacatahic; maui chupel, ma pu maixel vvach ahau, achih naol, ahuꜭhan;
sentences.l: not-was that it-is-lost there that it-goes, that it-is-fulfilled; not put-out, not also destroyed its-face lord, man wise-one, speaker;
sentences.i: it is not lost as it goes on, as it is fulfilled; the face of the lord, of the man of wisdom, of the orator, is not put out and not destroyed;
sentences.n: Two couplets. xma chi zach vi chi bec, chi ꜩacatahic 'it is not lost as it goes, as it is completed' (MS xmachi | zachvi): zach 'be lost', bec 'go', ꜩacatahic 'be completed, fulfilled', a passive in -atah (inferred; toggle by the letters). Brasseur: 'laquelle ne se perd point, mais se transmet avec la génération'. maui chupel, ma pu maixel 'not put out, nor destroyed': chupel is taken from chup 'go out, be extinguished', as a fire goes out, maixel from mai 'destroy (?)'; both inferred after Brasseur ('sans que s'éteigne ni s'anéantisse'). achih naol 'a man of wisdom'. ahuꜭhan is written with the g-shaped letter (MS ahughan), where three lines up the same word is ahuchan with plain ch; both are printed as written and the toggle follows each (ajuchan, ajuch'an), since the modern form is not known.

sentences.t: xa xchi canahic vmial, vꜭahol ta chuxoc.
sentences.l: only shall-remain his-daughter, his-son, so let-it-be.
sentences.i: his daughter and his son simply remain, and so it shall be.
sentences.n: xa xchi canahic 'it shall only remain': xchi- 'shall' + canah 'remain' + -ic. vmial, vꜭahol 'his daughter, his son' is a couplet: the father lives on in his children. The manuscript has vmial with i here, where it elsewhere has vmeal; the modern word is mi'al 'a man's daughter', and the toggle gives umi'al with the glottal stop restored (umeal keeps Ximénez's e). ta chuxoc 'so let it be' (ch- + ux 'become' + -oc).

sentences.t: Quehe mi xnu ban chave.
sentences.l: Thus just I-did to-you.
sentences.i: That is what I have done with you.
sentences.n: Quehe 'thus'. mi xnu ban 'I have just done' (mi + x- + nu- 'I' + ban 'do'). chave 'to you, with you'.

sentences.t: Cat acan cut chila chuvach vleu; maui ca camic.
sentences.l: You-climb then there on-its-face earth; not you-die.
sentences.i: Go up, then, there, onto the face of the earth; you shall not die.
sentences.n: Cat acan 'you go up': c- + at 'you' + acan 'climb, go up' (toggle kat aq'an). The manuscript clearly has t, where Brasseur reads Cal. chuvach vleu 'on the face of the earth': Xibalba is below, and the maiden is to go up to the world of people (inferred from acan 'go up'; Brasseur's note glosses 'sur la face de la terre' and asks whether the scene was set in a cave or underground). maui ca camic 'you shall not die': ca- (c- + a- 'you') + cam 'die' + -ic.

sentences.t: Cat oc pa ꜩih ta chuxoc,” xꜭha ri vholom Hunhunahpu, Vvcub Hunahpu.
sentences.l: You-enter in word, so let-it-be,” it-said the his-head Hunhunahpu, Vvcub Hunahpu.
sentences.i: Trust the word (?), and so it shall be,” said the head of Hunhunahpu and Vucub Hunahpu.
sentences.n: Cat oc pa ꜩih 'you enter into the word' (MS catoc | pa ꜩih, divided by us; Brasseur's OCR is garbled here): taken as 'trust the word' with Brasseur ('Crois en ma parole'), inferred. oc 'enter' (toggle ok). Here the manuscript has Hunhunahpu (written as two words, hun hunahpu) and Vvcub Hunahpu (vvcub hun|ahpu): the head speaks for both brothers (Brasseur: 'la tête de Hunhun-Ahpu et de Vukub-Hunahpu'; his note asks whether Vucub Hunahpu reappears here as the representative of the priestly order). xꜭha 'he said' is singular before the pair, as before.

sentences.t: Xavi qui naoh ta xqui bano are vꜩih Huracan, Chipi Caculha, Raxa Caculha chiquech.
sentences.l: Also their-thought when they-did-it, this its-word Huracan, Youngest Thunderbolt, Green Thunderbolt to-them.
sentences.i: It was by their own design that they did it, and it was the word of Huracan, Youngest Thunderbolt and Green Thunderbolt to them.
sentences.n: The narrator's comment. Xavi qui naoh 'just their thought': the two brothers acted of their own will. ta xqui bano 'when they did it' (x- + qui- 'they' + ban 'do' + -o). are vꜩih 'this (was) the word of': it was also the command of the three of the Heart of Sky of the first part, Huracan, Chipi Caculha and Raxa Caculha. chiquech 'to them'.

sentences.t: Quehe cu vꜩalihic chic capoh chi rochoch, quia pixab xbiyx chirech.
sentences.l: Thus then her-returning again maiden to her-home, many(?) counsels were-told to-her.
sentences.i: So the maiden went back to her home, and many counsels were told her.
sentences.n: vꜩalihic 'her returning': ꜩalih 'return' (the tzalij of an earlier part) + -ic. rochoch 'her home'. quia 'many' is inferred, as in an earlier part (Brasseur 'nombreux avertissements'). pixab 'counsel, instruction' (toggle pixab'). xbiyx 'it was said': biyh 'say' with the passive -x (Brasseur's OCR x-bivx). The head gave her more instructions than the text has told.

sentences.t: Huzu cu xvinaquir ral chupam rumal ri xa chub; are cut qui vinaquiric Hunahpu, Xbalanque.
sentences.l: Suddenly then it-came-into-being her-child inside-her by the only spittle; this then their coming-into-being Hunahpu, Xbalanque.
sentences.i: At once a child came into being within her, from the spittle alone; and this was the begetting of Hunahpu and Xbalanque.
sentences.n: Huzu 'at once' (huzuc, its c not written before cu; toggle jusuk, as in the last part). xvinaquir 'it came into being', the verb of the creation in the first part. ral 'her child': r- + al, a woman's child (as in Alom 'Mother of children'). chupam 'inside her'. rumal ri xa chub 'by the spittle only'. qui vinaquiric 'their coming into being': the two boys of the earlier parts, Hunahpu and Xbalanque, are conceived here.

sentences.t: Ta xopon cut chi rochoch ri capoh, xzacat cut vacaquib ic, ta xnauachil rumal vcahau, ri Cuchumaquic vbi vcahau.
sentences.l: When she-arrived then at her-home the maiden, they-passed(?) then six months, when she-was-noticed(?) by her-father, the Cuchumaquic his-name her-father.
sentences.i: When the maiden had come home and six months had passed, her father, whose name was Cuchumaquic, saw how it was with her.
sentences.n: xzacat 'passed' is a guess after Brasseur ('six mois s'étant écoulés'); the word is not otherwise known (toggle xsakat). vacaquib 'six': the modern word is waqib', here with an extra syllable (MS vacaquib, Brasseur vakakib, his k being q); the toggle gives q for the known word (waqaqib'). ic 'moon, month' (toggle ik'). xnauachil 'she was noticed': nau 'know' + vach 'face' + -il, inferred after Brasseur ('elle fut observée par son père'; toggle xnawachil).

sentences.t: Catepuch vnatahic capoh rumal vcahau, ta xil ri ral co chic.
sentences.l: Then-also her-being-noticed maiden by her-father, when he-saw the her-child there-is now.
sentences.i: Then the maiden was found out by her father, when he saw that she was with child.
sentences.n: A new paragraph in the manuscript (indented). Catepuch 'then also' (cate + puch, toggle K'atepuch). vnatahic 'her being noticed': nata 'remember, notice' + passive (inferred; Brasseur 'remarqua la jeune fille avec plus d'attention'). xil 'he saw' (x- + il 'see', no person written). ri ral co chic 'her child was there now': co is ꜭo 'there is' written with plain c (checked at 2.2×; Brasseur qo; toggle k'o).

sentences.t: Ta xqui cuch cut qui naoh conohel ahauab Huncame, Vvcub Came ruc ri Cuchumaquic.
sentences.l: Then they-joined then their-thought all lords Huncame, Vvcub Came with the Cuchumaquic.
sentences.i: Then all the lords, Huncame and Vucub Came, took counsel together with Cuchumaquic.
sentences.n: xqui cuch qui naoh 'they joined their thought', took counsel, the phrase of the first part (cuch 'join, gather'). ahauab 'lords' (ahau + plural -ab). Huncame and Vvcub Came are the two highest lords of Xibalba (One Death, Seven Death); the English spells Vucub, as in earlier parts. ruc 'with' is written with plain c (Brasseur ruq; toggle ruk').

sentences.t: “Are ri nu meal ꜭo chi ral, ix ahauab, xa vhoxbal,” xꜭha cu ri Cuchumaquic, ta xoponic cuꜭ ahauab.
sentences.l: “This the my-daughter there-is now her-child, you lords, only her-fornication,” he-said then the Cuchumaquic, when he-arrived with-them lords.
sentences.i: “This daughter of mine is with child, my lords; it is only from wantonness,” said Cuchumaquic when he came before the lords.
sentences.n: ꜭo chi ral 'her child is there', that is, she is with child (Brasseur's note: Areri nu meal qo chic ral); chi is chic 'now', its c not written (toggle chik). ix ahauab 'you lords'. vhoxbal 'her fornication': hox 'lie with, fornicate' + -bal, here the cause or means (inferred; Brasseur 'pour son déshonneur'); the same root gives hoxol 'one who fornicates' in ¶11 and ¶15 (toggle ujoxb'al). cuꜭ 'with them' (MS cug, read ꜭ).

sentences.t: “Vꜩ bala; cha coto vchi ri; ta ma cu biyh, chi puz cut, chi naht chi be puzo vi.”
sentences.l: “Good bala; you-dig-it her-mouth that; when not then she-tells, let-be-sacrificed then, far that (one)-goes to-sacrifice-her there.”
sentences.i: “Very well; probe her mouth; and if she does not tell, let her be sacrificed, let her be taken far away to be sacrificed.”
sentences.n: The lords answer. cha coto 'dig, open up' (ch- + a- 'you' + coto 'dig', the verb of an earlier part; Brasseur qoto): vchi ri 'her mouth', so 'make her speak' (Brasseur 'sonde sa bouche'). ta ma cu biyh 'if she does not tell' (biyh 'say, tell'; MS cu, Brasseur c'a). chi puz 'let (her) be sacrificed' (puz, inferred as in earlier parts). chi naht chi be puzo vi 'far away let (one) go to sacrifice her there': naht 'far'. puzo is written with o (Brasseur puzu): puz + -o, the transitive ending, so the one who goes is the sacrificer, not the maiden (Brasseur 'qu'on aille la sacrifier loin d'ici'; toggle puso).

sentences.t: “Vꜩ bala, alac ahauab,” xꜭha cut.
sentences.l: “Good bala, you(sirs) lords,” he-said then.
sentences.i: “Very well, my lords,” he said.
sentences.n: alac is the respectful 'you' for several people, the plural of lal (Brasseur's note: 'Alak est le pluriel du révérentiel lal'); alac ahauab is 'my lords'. The toggle gives alaq, the modern word, with Brasseur's k (= q).

sentences.t: Catecut xuꜩonoh chirech vmeal:
sentences.l: Then he-asked-it to-her his-daughter:
sentences.i: Then he asked his daughter:
sentences.n: xuꜩonoh 'he asked' (x- + v- + ꜩonoh 'ask'). chirech 'to her'. vmeal 'his daughter' (toggle umeal, as in ¶1).

sentences.t: “Apa ahchoce ri aval co cha pam, at nu meal?”
sentences.l: “Where whose the your-child there-is in-your belly, you my-daughter?”
sentences.i: “Whose is the child in your womb, my daughter?”
sentences.n: Apa ahchoce 'whose': apa 'where', ahchoce taken as ah- 'one who, owner' + choce 'whom (?)' (inferred; Brasseur 'De qui est l'enfant'). The manuscript writes ahchoce as one word (Brasseur ahchoke). aval 'your child' (a- 'your' + al). co cha pam 'is in your belly': co for ꜭo (plain c, Brasseur qo), cha for chi a- 'in your', pam 'belly, inside' (toggle k'o cha pam).

sentences.t: Xꜭha cut: “Mahabi val, lal nu cahau; mahabi achih vetaam vvach.”
sentences.l: She-said then: “Not-there-is my-child, you(sir) my-father; not-there-is man I-know his-face.”
sentences.i: She answered: “I have no child, my lord father; there is no man whose face I know.”
sentences.n: val 'my child' (v- 'my' + al). lal nu cahau 'my lord father': lal is the respectful 'you' (house table), cahau 'father'. mahabi achih vetaam vvach 'there is no man whose face I know': vetaam 'I know' (v- + etaam).

sentences.t: Xꜭha cut: “Vꜩ bala. Quiꜩih vi chi at hoxol.
sentences.l: He-said then: “Good bala. Truly there that you fornicator.
sentences.i: He said: “Very well. Truly, you are a wanton.
sentences.n: Quiꜩih vi chi at hoxol 'truly it is that you are a wanton': quiꜩih 'truly'; chi 'that'; at 'you'; hoxol, hox 'fornicate' + agent -ol, 'one who lies with men' (Brasseur 'une fornicatrice'; inferred, toggle joxol). The father does not believe her.

sentences.t: Chec, chi puzu, ix rahpop achih;
sentences.l: Take-her(?), sacrifice-her, you its-mat-lords of-men;
sentences.i: Carry her off, sacrifice her, you captains of the warriors;
sentences.n: He turns to the owls. Chec 'carry her off' follows Brasseur's note (ch- + ec, from ecah 'carry, bear on the shoulders'), inferred; toggle Chek by the letters. chi puzu 'sacrifice (her)': ch- + i- 'you (pl.)' + puz + -u. ix rahpop achih 'you captains of the warriors', the title of the owl messengers in an earlier part (inferred).

sentences.t: chi cama vloc ri vꜭux chupan zel; chi qui cololeh ahauab vacamic,” xe vꜭhax cut ri Tucur.
sentences.l: bring hither the her-heart inside bowl; you(?) return(?) lords today,” they-were-told then the Owl.
sentences.i: bring back her heart in a bowl, and come back to the lords this very day,” the owls were told.
sentences.n: chi cama vloc 'bring it here' (cama 'take', as the published kama; vloc 'hither'). vꜭux 'her heart' (MS q-shaped qux, read ꜭ). zel 'bowl': a gourd bowl or vessel, after Brasseur ('un vase'); the toggle respells the letters (sel). chi qui cololeh ahauab 'return to the lords' follows Brasseur ('soyez de retour aujourd'hui avec les rois'), inferred: in ¶14 the messengers repeat the order as xchi qui ꜩololeh ahauab with the tz ligature, the ꜩalih 'return' of ¶9, and cololeh with plain c may be the same word. qui is taken as 'you (pl.)' with Brasseur (inferred). xe vꜭhax 'they were told'. Tucur, the owls, singular for the kind, as in an earlier part (toggle Tukur).

sentences.t: E cahib ta xebec qui tiquem ri zel; ta xebec qui chelem ri capoh, cucaam ri Zaquitoc, puzbal re.
sentences.l: They four when they-went their-lifting(?) the bowl; when they-went their-carrying(?) the maiden, carrying-it(?) the Zaquitoc, instrument-of-sacrifice of-her.
sentences.i: There were four of them, and they went and took up the bowl; they went and carried off the maiden, taking with them Zaquitoc, the blade for her sacrifice.
sentences.n: A couplet: xebec qui tiquem ri zel; xebec qui chelem ri capoh 'they went to their taking up of the bowl, they went to their carrying of the maiden'. qui tiquem and qui chelem are verbal nouns in -em with qui- 'their' (MS quiti|quem). Both verbs are inferred from Brasseur ('allèrent prendre le vase … portant la jeune fille sur leurs épaules'). cucaam 'carrying it' is taken as c- + v- (singular, the four not marked) + cam 'take' with a long vowel (inferred; Brasseur cu caam); the toggle respells the letters. Zaquitoc was the name of the torch of Xibalba in an earlier part, zaqui 'white' + toc, which Brasseur takes as 'flint'; here it is the white flint knife (Brasseur 'un couteau de silex'), kept as a name. puzbal re 'her instrument of sacrifice': puz + -bal, the instrument, + re 'of her' (toggle pusb'al).

sentences.t: “Maui chuꜩinic quinicamizah, ix zamahel, rumal maui nu hoxbal ri ꜭo chi nu pam;
sentences.l: “Not it-comes-right you-kill-me, you messengers, because not my-fornication the there-is in my-belly;
sentences.i: “You cannot kill me, messengers, for what is in my womb is not from any wantonness of mine;
sentences.n: Maui chuꜩinic 'it will not come right', it cannot be (xuꜩinic 'it succeeded' in an earlier part). quinicamizah 'you (pl.) kill me' (MS quinicami|zah, one word; Brasseur qu'in y camizah): c- + in 'me' + i- 'you (pl.)' + camiza, cam 'die' + -iza, 'cause to die', + -h (toggle kinikamisaj). zamahel 'messengers', as in the last parts. nu hoxbal 'my fornication', as vhoxbal in ¶10. ꜭo chi nu pam 'which is in my belly'.

sentences.t: xaqui xvinaquiric, xere xbe nu maihah ri vholom Hunhunahpu, ꜭo chi Pucbal Chah.
sentences.l: simply it-came-into-being, just-when I-went my-marvelling the his-head Hunhunahpu, there-is at Pucbal Chah.
sentences.i: it simply came into being when I went to marvel at the head of Hunhunahpu that is at Pucbal Chah.
sentences.n: xaqui 'simply, merely' (xa + qui; Brasseur xaki 'seul'), inferred, toggle by the letters. xvinaquiric 'it came into being'. xere xbe nu maihah 'just when I went to marvel': nu maihah 'my marvelling at', the maihah of ¶2. Here the manuscript has Hunhunahpu.

sentences.t: Queque ta cut maui qui puz, ix zamahel,” xꜭha ri capoh ta xꜭhauic.
sentences.l: Thus (ta) then not you-sacrifice(-me), you messengers,” she-said the maiden when she-spoke.
sentences.i: So you shall not sacrifice me, messengers,” said the maiden as she spoke to them.
sentences.n: Queque is printed as written (MS quequetacut, read at 1.8×); it is presumably a slip for quehe 'thus' (Brasseur quehe-ta-cut), but the correction is not certain, so the print stands and the toggle respells the letters (Keke). quehe ta cut 'so then'. maui qui puz 'you shall not sacrifice (me)': qui is taken as c- + i- 'you (pl.)', with 'me' understood (Brasseur 'vous ne me sacrifierez point'; inferred). xꜭhauic 'she spoke'.

sentences.t: “Naquipa xchi ca coh vꜫexel ri iꜭux?
sentences.l: “What shall we-put its-replacement the your-heart?
sentences.i: “What shall we put in place of your heart?
sentences.n: The messengers answer. xchi ca coh 'we shall put': xchi- + ca- 'we' + coh 'put' (as in the sixth part). vꜫexel 'its replacement, something in exchange', the house rendering (MS vquexel, the q-shaped letter + u read as the tresillo with Brasseur's u gexel; toggle uq'exel as in the sixth part). iꜭux 'your heart' with i-, the plural 'your': the owls speak to the maiden in the respectful plural (Brasseur's note on this line), while a cahau 'your father' below is singular.

sentences.t: Mi xbiyx vloc rumal a cahau: Chi cam vloc ri vꜭux; xchi qui ꜩololeh ahauab;
sentences.l: Just it-was-said hither by your-father: Let-bring hither the her-heart; you-shall return lords;
sentences.i: This was the word just given us by your father: Bring back her heart; you shall return to the lords;
sentences.n: Mi xbiyx vloc 'it has just been said': mi + x- + biyh 'say' + passive -x. The father's order follows, set after a colon as in the establishment (no inner quotation marks). Chi cam vloc 'bring hither' (cam 'take', toggle k'am, as in the last parts). xchi qui ꜩololeh ahauab 'you shall return to the lords': ꜩololeh taken as the ꜩalih 'return' of ¶9 (inferred; the modern verb is tzolij); compare cololeh in ¶11.

sentences.t: xchi qui ꜩacuixtah, xchi qui hunam vachih vꜩaquic;
sentences.l: you-shall ꜩacuixtah(?), you-shall together effort(?) its-completion;
sentences.i: you shall make it certain (?), you shall show together that it is done (?);
sentences.n: A couplet, both lines unclear. xchi qui ꜩacuixtah is a doubtful reading: at 3.5× the letters after ꜩa are not clear (c or a second a, then u i x), and Brasseur reads tzakix-tah; the meaning is not known ('make it certain' is a guess after Brasseur's 'soyez formels'). In the next xchi a blot covers the x or c. hunam 'alike, together'; vachih is the 'effort' of an earlier part (inferred); vꜩaquic 'its completion' is a doubtful reading (Brasseur's OCR u wakit), taken from ꜩac 'complete', as ꜩacatahic in ¶7 (a guess; Brasseur 'manifestez-en l'accomplissement'). The toggle respells the letters.

sentences.t: chanim chi cama vloc pa zel, chi coloba; cahoc vꜭux chupan zel.
sentences.l: quickly bring hither in bowl, set-it(?); downward her-heart inside bowl.
sentences.i: bring it back quickly in a bowl, set it in place (?); her heart down inside the bowl.
sentences.n: chanim 'quickly, at once'. chi cama vloc pa zel 'bring it in a bowl'. chi coloba is taken as col 'set, put in place' + -oba (a guess; Brasseur leaves it out); the same root may be in xucolo and colom in ¶16. cahoc 'downward', to the bottom (cah 'go down' + -oc; Brasseur 'au fond du vase').

sentences.t: Ma pa mi xoh vꜭhax vloc?
sentences.l: Not (pa) just we-were-told hither?
sentences.i: Were we not told so?
sentences.n: Ma … pa 'is it not …?' xoh vꜭhax 'we were spoken to': xoh 'we' (the absolutive) + vꜭhax, the passive of ꜭha 'speak'.

sentences.t: Naquila cut xchi ca ya pa zel?
sentences.l: Anything then shall we-give in bowl?
sentences.i: What then shall we put in the bowl?
sentences.n: Naquila 'what, anything'. xchi ca ya 'we shall give, put'.

sentences.t: Ca cah ta na bec, ma ta cat camic,” xeꜭha cu ri zamahel.
sentences.l: We(?)-want (ta) first you(?)-go, not (ta) you-die,” they-said then the messengers.
sentences.i: We would rather you went on your way and did not die,” said the messengers.
sentences.n: A doubtful division (MS cacahtanabec mata cat camic; Brasseur ca k'ah-ta mabec ma-ta Cat camic): ca is taken as the ongoing c- with its vowel, and cah as c- 'we' (the form before a vowel) + ah 'want', the qaj 'we want' of an earlier part (inferred; toggle ka qaj); ta … ta mark the wish; bec 'go'. ma ta cat camic 'that you do not die'. Brasseur: 'cependant nous aimerions mieux que tu ne meures point'. xeꜭha 'they said'.

sentences.t: “Vꜩ bala. Maui quech ri ꜭux ta chuxoc; ruꜭ maui varal ivochoch chuxic;
sentences.l: “Good bala. Not theirs the heart so let-it-be; with-it not here your-home it-shall-be;
sentences.i: “Very well. This heart shall not be theirs, and your home shall not be here;
sentences.n: The maiden answers. Maui quech ri ꜭux 'the heart shall not be theirs', the lords' (quech 'theirs'). ruꜭ maui 'and also not' (MS rug, read ꜭ): ruꜭ 'with it', joining the second line. ivochoch 'your (pl.) home': iv- + ochoch. chuxic 'it shall be', beside chuxoc. She promises the owls that they shall not have to stay in Xibalba.

sentences.t: ma cu xa chi chih vinac chi camic;
sentences.l: not then only that you-bear(?) people to death;
sentences.i: nor shall you only drive (?) people to their death;
sentences.n: A difficult line (Brasseur: 'cette phrase est d'une extrême difficulté'). ma cu xa 'and not only'. chi chih is taken as chi + chih 'bear, endure' of an earlier part, with the 'you (pl.)' of Brasseur's ch'y (chi + i-), not written here (inferred; Brasseur 'vous aurez en votre pouvoir'), and 'drive' is a guess. vinac chi camic 'people to death'.

sentences.t: cate quiꜩih ivech ri quiꜩih hoxol, cate naipu vech Huncame, Vvcub Came;
sentences.l: then truly yours the true fornicators, then likewise mine Huncame, Vvcub Came;
sentences.i: the true wantons shall be truly yours, and Huncame and Vucub Came shall be mine;
sentences.n: A couplet: cate … ivech 'then … yours (pl.)', cate naipu vech 'then likewise mine'. ri quiꜩih hoxol 'the true fornicators', the word the father threw at her in ¶11: the guilty shall belong to the owls, and the lords to her (inferred, after Brasseur). naipu 'likewise' (toggle naypu).

sentences.t: xa quic, xa holomax rech ta chuxoc; are chicut chuvach.
sentences.l: only blood, only holomax(?) his so let-it-be; this again-then before-his-face.
sentences.i: only blood, only holomax (?) shall be his; that is what shall be set before him.
sentences.n: xa quic, xa holomax rech 'only blood, only holomax (shall be) his', the lord's. holomax is not understood: it has the letters of holom 'head' + -ax (in the manuscript a blot covers lo); Brasseur's note takes it as 'to be at the head, to rule', or with quic as the name of an illness, and he renders 'le sang seul passe contrat pour lui-même'. It comes back in ¶16 as part of the sap's name. It is left in K'iche' in the English. are chicut chuvach 'that, then, before his face' (chicut 'again then', toggle chik'ut).

sentences.t: Maui are ri ꜭux chi cat chuvach ta chuxoc.
sentences.l: Not this the heart that it-burns before-his-face so let-it-be.
sentences.i: It shall not be the heart that burns before him.
sentences.n: chi cat 'that it burn': cat 'burn' (plain c; Brasseur qat), the cat of an earlier part, toggle k'at as there, not kat 'you'. The maiden knows what the lords will do with the heart (¶18).

sentences.t: Chi coho ri vvach che,” ꜭha cut ri capoh.
sentences.l: Put-it the its-fruit tree,” says then the maiden.
sentences.i: Put in the fruit of the tree,” said the maiden.
sentences.n: Chi coho 'put it in' (coh 'put' + -o). ri vvach che 'the fruit of the tree', here what the tree gives, its sap. ꜭha cut 'she says then' has no x before ꜭha: the manuscript begins the line with ghacut and the line above ends with che, so the completive is not written. It is printed as written (Brasseur cha-cut).

sentences.t: Ꜫaꜫ cut vvaal ri che xelic, xcul pa zel.
sentences.l: Red then its-sap the tree it-came-out, it-ran(?) in bowl.
sentences.i: Red was the sap that came out of the tree, and it ran into the bowl.
sentences.n: Ꜫaꜫ 'red' is written with two clear tresillos (checked at 4×), where Brasseur reads cak 'red'. The same spelling is the word for fire in ¶18–19 (Brasseur gag there). The modern word for red is kaq; the toggle respells the letters (q'aq'), as an earlier part's ꜫaꜫa 'red' (q'aq'a). vvaal 'its liquid', the sap (vaal 'water, juice', as in an earlier part). xelic 'it came out' (el 'go out' + -ic). xcul 'it ran in': with pa zel 'into the bowl' it is taken as 'come, flow' (Brasseur 'coula'), not the xcul 'it was smeared' of an earlier part, though the letters and the toggle (xkul) are the same; inferred.

sentences.t: Catepuch xuvon rib, coloquic xuxic, vꜫexel vꜭux, ta iiꜩ chi cul vvaal cac che.
sentences.l: Then-also it-thickened(?) itself, round it-became, its-replacement her-heart, when iiꜩ(?) that it-comes its-sap red tree.
sentences.i: Then it thickened (?) and became round, in place of her heart, as the sap of the red tree came welling (?) out.
sentences.n: Catepuch 'then also' (Brasseur leaves it out). xuvon rib 'it … itself': von is not otherwise known; 'thickened' follows Brasseur ('elle se coagula'), a guess (toggle xuwon). coloquic xuxic 'it became round' (coloquic 'round', a guess as in an earlier part). vꜫexel vꜭux 'in place of her heart'. ta iiꜩ chi cul is a doubtful reading: two minims before the ꜩ, with a mark above (Brasseur ta yitz chi c'ul); 'welling out' follows Brasseur ('qui sortait jaillissant'), a guess. cul 'it comes' (c- + ul). cac che 'red tree' is written with plain c (MS cac, where the lines around have tresillos; Brasseur cak); the toggle gives kaq, the modern word for red, which these letters spell without restoring anything (Brasseur's cak, his k being q, agrees); ꜫaꜫ with tresillos is respelled q'aq' letter for letter.

sentences.t: Queheri quic vvaal che xelic vꜫexel vquiquel; ta xucolo chila ri quic chupan ri vvaal ꜫaꜫ che.
sentences.l: Like blood its-sap tree it-came-out, its-replacement her-blood; when it-set(?) there the blood inside the its-sap red tree.
sentences.i: Like blood the sap of the tree came out, in place of her blood; and the blood set (?) there inside, the sap of the red tree.
sentences.n: Queheri quic 'like blood'. vquiquel 'her blood': v- + quic 'blood' + -el (toggle ukik'el, with the ejective of the known word kik'). xucolo 'it set it (there)' is a guess after Brasseur ('il se figea là'); col may be the root of chi coloba in ¶14 (toggle xukolo). chupan 'inside' (toggle chupam). ri vvaal ꜫaꜫ che 'the sap of the red tree' stands beside quic 'blood': the sap is the blood.

sentences.t: Quehe curi quic rih xuxic, ꜫaꜫluhluh chic, colom chi pa zel, ta xcopcot ri che rumal capoh.
sentences.l: Thus then blood its-surface it-became, red-gleaming now, set(?) (chi) in bowl, when it-became-renowned(?) the tree because-of maiden.
sentences.i: So its surface became blood, glistening red, set (?) in the bowl, and the tree became renowned (?) because of the maiden.
sentences.n: quic rih xuxic 'its back, its surface became blood' (rih 'its back'). ꜫaꜫluhluh 'glistening red' is ꜫaꜫ 'red' + luhluh, a doubled ending of appearance (inferred; Brasseur cakluhluh 'brillante, rougeâtre'); MS tresillos, toggle q'aq'lujluj by the letters. colom 'set, lying' (a guess, as xucolo). colom chi pa zel 'set in the bowl' (Brasseur 'coagulée dans le vase'). xcopcot is not otherwise known; it is rendered with Brasseur ('tandis que l'arbre devenait célèbre à cause de la jeune fille'), a guess: the form has no person prefix, and rumal capoh can be 'because of the maiden' or 'by the maiden', so a passive 'it was cut' would also fit the grammar, but nothing here supports that sense (toggle xkopkot).

sentences.t: Chuh Ꜫaꜫ Che chuꜭhaxic.
sentences.l: Chuh Red Tree it-is-called.
sentences.i: It is called Chuh Q'aq' Che, the red tree.
sentences.n: The tree's name. Brasseur's note: the Quichés call chuh-cakche the tree the French call sang-dragon, 'dragon's blood' (the Mexicans' ezquahuitl, 'blood tree'), and chuh is cochineal, the red dye insect. That chuh is cochineal is his reading (inferred). Ꜫaꜫ Che 'red tree' (tresillos as above). The name is kept in the English, in modern letters. chuꜭhaxic 'it is called'.

sentences.t: Are curi quic xubinaah, rumal quic holomax chuchaxic.
sentences.l: This then blood he-named-it, because blood holomax(?) it-is-called.
sentences.i: And so it was given the name of blood, because it is called blood holomax (?).
sentences.n: xubinaah 'he named it' (bi 'name' + -naah, inferred; Brasseur 'surnommé'). quic holomax: the words of ¶15 (holomax not understood; Brasseur 'sang passé en contrat'). chuchaxic is written with plain ch (MS, Brasseur ch'u chaxic), the house word chuꜭhaxic as in an earlier part (toggle chuch'axik).

sentences.t: “Chila cut quix locox vi; chuvach vleu ꜭo ivech chuxic,” xꜭha cut chique ri Tucur.
sentences.l: “There then you-are-loved(?) there; on-face earth there-is yours it-shall-be,” she-said then to-them the Owl.
sentences.i: “There you shall be loved (?); on the face of the earth there shall be a portion for you,” she said to the owls.
sentences.n: quix locox vi (MS quix | locoxvi): quix 'you (pl.)', c- + ix; locox is not otherwise known and 'be loved' is inferred from Brasseur ('vous serez aimés'), who reads logox (his g is ꜫ); the toggle respells the letters. chuvach vleu ꜭo ivech chuxic 'on the face of the earth there shall be what is yours': Brasseur 'deviendra votre héritage'. ivech 'yours (pl.)'.

sentences.t: “Vꜩ bala, at capoh. Xca beba; ca naba acan oc; xa ca bin apan oc;
sentences.l: “Good bala, you maiden. We-go(?); we naba(?) up (oc); only you-walk away (oc);
sentences.i: “Very well, maiden. We are going (?); we shall go up (?); and you, just walk on your way;
sentences.n: Xca beba; ca naba acan oc (MS xcabeba canaba a|canoc; Brasseur X-ka pe ba, ka yapa akan-oc): a doubtful reading, the b and n as written. Xca beba is taken as x- + ca- 'we' + be 'go' + -ba (a guess); ca naba acan oc as ca- 'we' + naba (not known) + acan oc 'upward' (a guess; Brasseur 'nous allons rendre compte'). xa ca bin apan oc 'just walk away': ca- (c- + a- 'you') + bin 'walk' + apan oc 'away, over there' (Brasseur 'va ton chemin').

sentences.t: oh na ca yaix tah vva vꜫexevach a ꜭux chi qui vach ahauab,” xeꜭha cut ri zamahel.
sentences.l: we first we-give(?) (tah) its-face its-replacement-face your-heart before their face lords,” they-said then the messengers.
sentences.i: we, for our part, shall set the likeness and the stand-in of your heart before the eyes of the lords,” said the messengers.
sentences.n: oh na 'we, for our part' (na 'first'). ca yaix tah is taken from ya 'give, put' (MS ohnacaya|ixtah; inferred). vva vꜫexevach 'its face, its exchange-face': vva for vvach 'its face' (as in an earlier part), vꜫexevach is vꜫexel 'replacement' joined to vach 'face', the stand-in that looks like the heart (MS vquexevach, read with Brasseur's gexevach; toggle uq'exewach). chi qui vach ahauab 'before the lords' faces'.

sentences.t: Ta xopon cut chi qui vach ahauab; que zelevachin conohel.
sentences.l: When they-arrived then before their face lords; they zelevachin(?) all.
sentences.i: When they came before the lords, all of them were waiting and watching (?).
sentences.n: que 'they' (c- + e) with a verb of state. zelevachin is not otherwise known; it contains vach 'face, eye', and 'waiting and watching' follows Brasseur ('dans une attente inquiète'), a guess (toggle selewachin).

sentences.t: “Maui xuꜩinic?” xꜭha cut Huncame.
sentences.l: “Not it-came-right?” he-said then Huncame.
sentences.i: “Is it done?” said Huncame.
sentences.n: Maui xuꜩinic 'has it not come right?', that is, is it done (xuꜩinic 'it succeeded, was completed').

sentences.t: “Mi xuꜩinic, ix ahauab; va na cu vꜭux xe ꜭo pa zel.”
sentences.l: “Just it-came-right, you lords; this now then her-heart bottom there-is in bowl.”
sentences.i: “It is done, my lords; here is her heart at the bottom of the bowl.”
sentences.n: Mi xuꜩinic 'it has just been done'. va na cu 'here now'. xe ꜭo pa zel 'at the bottom, in the bowl': xe 'root, foot, bottom' (Brasseur 'au fond de ce vase'; toggle xe').

sentences.t: “Vꜩ bala; vila cut,” xꜭha cu ri Huncame.
sentences.l: “Good bala; I-see-it then,” he-said then the Huncame.
sentences.i: “Very well; let me see it,” said Huncame.
sentences.n: vila 'I see it, let me see' (v- 'I' + il + -a), as in ¶3 (Brasseur 'que je le voie donc').

sentences.t: Ta xuchuieh cu acan oc; ta turur rih chi comah, ꜫaꜫluhluh rih chi quic.
sentences.l: Then he-lifted-it(?) then up (oc); when turur(?) its-surface with comah(?), red-gleaming its-surface with blood.
sentences.i: He lifted it up (?), and its surface welled (?) with comah (?), glistening red with blood.
sentences.n: xuchuieh 'he lifted it' is a guess after Brasseur ('il le souleva délicatement du bout des doigts'); with acan oc 'upward'. A couplet: turur rih chi comah, ꜫaꜫluhluh rih chi quic 'its surface … with comah, its surface glistening red with blood'. The first letter of turur is heavily overwritten, read t (Brasseur ca turur-rih), a doubtful reading; turur and comah are not otherwise known, and 'welled' is a guess after Brasseur ('commença à se répandre'). comah is left in K'iche'.

sentences.t: “Vꜩ chi luu vvach ꜫaꜫ; chi ya chuvi ꜫaꜫ,” xꜭha cut Huncame.
sentences.l: “Good that you-stir(?) its-face fire; put on-top fire,” he-said then Huncame.
sentences.i: “Stir up the fire well, and put it on the fire,” said Huncame.
sentences.n: Vꜩ chi luu vvach ꜫaꜫ 'well stir (?) the face of the fire' (MS chiluu): luu is not otherwise known, and 'stir up' follows Brasseur ('Avivez bien les braises'), a guess. ꜫaꜫ 'fire', with tresillos (Brasseur gag). chi ya chuvi ꜫaꜫ 'put it on top of the fire' (chuvi 'on top of').

sentences.t: Catepuch xqui chaquih chuvi ꜫaꜫ, coc cut xqui na Xibalba;
sentences.l: Then-also they-dried-it on-top fire, smell(?) then they-felt Xibalba;
sentences.i: Then they parched it over the fire, and Xibalba caught the smell (?);
sentences.n: xqui chaquih 'they dried it': chaquih 'dry' (as in an earlier part) used as a verb (inferred; Brasseur 'jeté sur le feu'). coc is taken as 'smell, fragrance' with Brasseur ('commencé à sentir l'odeur'), inferred, toggle by the letters. xqui na 'they felt, perceived' (na 'feel', the root of nao). Xibalba 'the people of Xibalba'.

sentences.t: xe quiz yacatah vloc conohel, xe chique chuvi;
sentences.l: they-finished-rising hither all, they chique(?) over-it;
sentences.i: they all rose up together and leaned (?) over it;
sentences.n: xe quiz yacatah vloc 'they all rose at once' (MS xequiz yacatah): quiz 'finish, all', yacatah 'rise, be lifted' (yac 'lift' + -atah; Brasseur 'tous se levèrent à la fois'), inferred. xe chique chuvi: chique is not clear here; 'leaned over it' is a guess (Brasseur 'se tournèrent … vers le parfum'). The toggle respells the letters.

sentences.t: quiꜩih chi quz xqui nao ri vzibel quic.
sentences.l: truly that sweet(?) they-felt-it the its-smoke blood.
sentences.i: truly sweet they found the smoke of the blood.
sentences.n: quiꜩih chi quz 'truly sweet': quz as in ¶3 and ¶4, with plain qu where Brasseur has guz (inferred). xqui nao 'they felt it' (na + -o). vzibel 'its smoke': zib 'smoke' + -el (Brasseur u zibel; toggle usib'el).

sentences.t: Arecut e chiquichoh vi canoc, ta xebe ri Tucur e uabai rech capoh;
sentences.l: This-then they chiquichoh(?) there remaining, when they-went the Owl, they uabai(?) of maiden;
sentences.i: And while they stayed there, entranced (?), the owls went off, the maiden's escort (?);
sentences.n: e chiquichoh vi canoc 'they (were) … there, left behind': chiquichoh is not otherwise known (Brasseur 'tandis qu'ils demeuraient'); 'entranced' is a guess. canoc 'left behind, remaining'. xebe 'they went'. e uabai rech capoh 'they (were) the … of the maiden': uabai is not otherwise known; 'escort' is a guess, taken with vabanel below (Brasseur 'prévenus par la jeune fille'). The manuscript writes u (e uabai), Brasseur e vabai; the toggle respells the letters.

sentences.t: xu quia acan oc chi hul chuvi vleuh;
sentences.l: she(?) many(?) climbed up (oc) at hole on-top earth;
sentences.i: and she went up (?) out of the hole onto the earth;
sentences.n: xu quia acan oc chi hul chuvi vleuh: xu is taken as x- + v-; quia is the 'many' of ¶9 (inferred); acan oc 'up', as in ¶5 and ¶7. Brasseur renders 'montant en grand nombre de la fondrière vers la terre'. The third letter of acanoc is tall and uncertain (MS xuquia a?anoc), and a blot covers the letters after chuv (Brasseur chuvi e); chuvi 'on top of' is the most likely reading. Both are doubtful. hul 'pit, hollow': the way up from Xibalba. vleuh 'earth', with Ximénez's final h.

sentences.t: xzalih chi cu cahoc ri vabanel.
sentences.l: it-returned again then downward the vabanel(?).
sentences.i: and her escort (?) went back down again.
sentences.n: xzalih is taken as ꜩalih 'return' (vꜩalihic in ¶9) written with the plain z (inferred; Brasseur x-zalih); no plural e- is written, so vabanel is taken as one body, her escort; the toggle respells the letters (xsalij). chi cu 'again then': chic with its c shared with cu (toggle chik). cahoc 'downward'. vabanel is not otherwise known, perhaps the same word as uabai above ('escort, those who went with her' is a guess; Brasseur 'ses partisans').

sentences.t: Quehe cut xe chacatah vi rahaual Xibalba ri rumal capoh; xe moyvachixic conohel.
sentences.l: Thus then they-were-brought-low there its-lords Xibalba the by maiden; they-were-blinded all.
sentences.i: So the lords of Xibalba were brought low by a maiden; they were all blinded.
sentences.n: The episode ends. xe chacatah vi 'they were brought low there' (MS xe | chacatahvi), the word of the downfall of Vucub Caquix and of the brothers in the earlier parts. rahaual Xibalba 'the lords of Xibalba'. xe moyvachixic 'they were blinded, deceived': moy 'blind, dim' + vach 'face, eye' + passive -ix + -ic, 'their eyes were darkened' (inferred; Brasseur 'tous se laissèrent aveugler'; toggle moywachixik). The next part begins with Xquic coming to the grandmother.
